title: Meridian Utilities VPC preflight blueprint and TF adapters (WIP)
body:
Purpose
----
This is a working preflight blueprint for the Meridian Utilities private deployment. Goal: produce a verified on-prem/VPC deployment path and a small set of Terraform adapter modules so the customer can: 1) onboard a constrained three-node cluster for pilot, 2) scale to a production 10+ node pool, and 3) perform a zero-downtime runtime/TF upgrade in their environment.

Scope (what this doc is trying to cover)
- Network and routing assumptions for Meridian's existing VPC (MPLS/Transit gateway)
- Compact hardware sizing for pilot vs. production, with token/sec and storage assumptions
- TF adapter design: how to map Redwood Dedicated modules to Meridian infra (BMC, VLANs, NSG rules)
- Upgrade and rollback plan for both runtime and TF modules
- Testing/validation matrix and preflight checklist for ops handoff

Out-of-scope
- Deep dive into Meridian's customer data lifecycle policies (we'll defer to security team for final compliance mapping)
- Procurement and rack-level cabling plans

High-level customer context
- Industry: regional utilities (smart-meter gateway ingestion, outage support chatbots)
- Data sensitivity: PII-lite, regulated by local utility privacy policy; they require customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs forwarded to Splunk
- Current infra: three regional VPCs connected by a transit gateway; on-prem colocation in one region with existing BMC and VLAN segmentation.

Assumptions (validated in initial call 2025-07-29)
- Meridian will provide a bastion host + jump keys for initial deployment windows.
- IP plan: 10.240.0.0/16 reserved for Redwood subnets inside the Meridian transit VPC.
- K8s: they will run EKS-on-prem variant (customer-managed control plane) or equivalent; Redwood runtime will be deployed inside customer k8s as containers backed by GPUs (NVIDIA A100 or H100) where available.
- Storage: a dedicated NVMe-backed node pool for model artifacts and KV cache; replicated across AZs if available.
- Audit: audit logs will be forwarded via TLS to central Splunk collector (syslog-ng).

Sizing summary
- Pilot (3-node):
  - Node type: 1 x mgmt (4 vCPU, 16GB), 2 x worker (32 vCPU, 512GB RAM, 2x NVMe 4TB) each with 1 x A10/A30 or a single shared 80GB HBM GPU attachment (depending on procurement)
  - Expected throughput: ~6 concurrent medium-length (1k tokens) requests; baseline 8–12 tokens/sec per GPU, ~480–720 tokens/sec overall with effective batching and KV caching
  - Disk: 6TB usable NVMe per worker (RAID0 across 2 drives for perf), snapshot to S3-compatible object store nightly
- Production (10-node):
  - Node type: 2 x infra (16 vCPU, 64GB), 8 x worker (64 vCPU, 1TB RAM, NVMe 8TB) each with 1 x H100 or 2 x A100 depending on cost profile
  - Expected throughput: baseline 3k–5k tokens/sec for typical mix; peak burst capacity handled by autoscaling policies and a small hosted fallthrough route
  - Network: 25 Gbps baseline between nodes; recommend 40 Gbps uplink on worker pool for KV sync and model sharding

Why these numbers
- We sized around median model used in Meridian pilot (open LLaMA-variant, 13B) with quantization to 4-bit and KV caching for repeated session traffic.
- NVMe working set reduces model load times from cold-starts; we expect warm cache hit rates >65% in typical usage leading to 2–3x effective throughput improvement over cold starts.

Terraform adapter design (proposal)
- Goal: provide small set of adapter modules that map Redwood's canonical modules to Meridian's naming, BMC interaction, and network constructs. Avoid changing Redwood core modules; use adapter wrapping.
- Proposed modules:
  1) meridian_vpc_adapter: maps redwood_vpc inputs to Meridian subnet/VLANs and creates NAT/route table hooks for transit gateway
  2) meridian_gpu_node_pool: wrapper around redwood_node_pool with extra tags, BMC bootstrapping script integration, and PXE fingerprint tests
  3) meridian_storage_profile: creates NVMe volumes, sets local SSD encryption keys using customer KMS via external provider
  4) meridian_kms_integration: vault-based key rotation policy and HSM connector configs (PKCS#11 shim where required)
- Pattern: keep adapters thin; accept same inputs as redwood modules where possible, provide meridian-specific defaults.
- Example input mapping note: redwood_node_pool.cpu_profile -> meridian_gpu_node_pool.cpu_class (values: compute-64, compute-32)

Upgrade/rollout strategy (runtime + TF)
- Principles: zero customer-visible downtime for read-serving, graceful degradation for write-heavy background jobs, rollbackable TF changes within 30 minutes.
- Staged rollout plan:
  1) Preflight validation (static checks + dry-run TF apply in staging sandbox)
  2) Canary (pilot cluster nodes): deploy runtime image update to 10% of workers using nodeSelector + cordon/drain strategy, run smoke and perf tests for 2h
  3) Gradual rollout: increment to 30%, 60%, 100% with automated perf gates (latency p95 < baseline * 1.25, token error rate < 0.5%)
  4) TF module upgrade: apply adapter changes with plan review; use state locking and apply to infra nodes labeled 'tf-canary' first. Keep a companion branch with original state for quick reapply.
  5) Rollback: use stored golden images and TF state snapshot; snapshot S3-compatible backend before apply.

Validation & test matrix (what to run at each phase)
- Static checks:
  - TF fmt and validate, module input schema check, network CIDR conflict scan
- Functional checks (post-apply):
  - K8s nodes join and GPU drivers present
  - Redis/KV cache warm-up scenario (simulate 1000 unique sessions)
  - Model load+inference P50/P95 latency measurements for 10k sample prompts
- Security checks:
  - KMS key rotation test, HSM signing test, audit log ingestion to Splunk validated for 24h

Preflight checklist (must be green before pilot deploy)
- [ ] Meridian infra provides BMC credentials and maintenance window for initial booting (owner: Meridian infra)
- [ ] IP allocation confirmed and documented (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] HSM connector certs exchanged and tested (owner: Priya)
- [ ] TF adapter repo branch created and reviewed (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Compliance kickoff with security (owner: Evan)

Open questions / decisions required
- GPU procurement: Meridian is evaluating A30 vs. H100 for production. Need final decision for driver tuning and kernel selection (JIRA: PD-7051).
- Backup SLA: How long do we keep NVMe snapshots in object store? Current ask: 30 days, but costs may push down to 7 days. Ops to decide.
- Network egress controls: Meridian wants aggressive egress rules; verify that Redwood fallback endpoints for hosted failover can be whitelisted via IP ranges.

Risk register (top 3)
- KMS/HSM integration delays -> blocks rollout (mitigation: parallelize connector test before TF apply)
- Unexpected model cold-start costs on 13B when quantization fails for some artifacts -> mitigation: extra worker reserved for pre-warm and caching tuning
- TF state drift from manual changes -> mitigation: enable strict RBAC and restrict terraform apply to SRE group, run drift detection weekly

Operational runbook excerpts (for on-call SRE)
- GPU OOM or driver crash: cordon affected node, force-delete pods after 5m, reprovision using PXE reboot script (link to PXE script in repo).
- Slow KV replication: check NVMe I/O metrics, promote secondary local cache, open PD-7063 to investigate kernel-level I/O tuning.

Action items (next 2 weeks)
- Diego: branch adapter modules, stub out meridian_kms_integration (due 2026-03-05) [JIRA PD-7032]
- Priya: schedule HSM cert exchange and run handshake test (due 2026-03-02)
- Evan: prepare performance harness for pilot model (generate load profile and token distribution) (due 2026-03-07)
- Aisha: finalize preflight checklist and book Meridian windows (due 2026-03-01)

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep adapter module small; customer doesn't want to absorb heavy diverging TF logic. We should upstream any generic helpers back into redwood modules.
- Consider adding an experimental 'warm-up' init container that pulls popular models into local NVMe on node boot (helps warm cache during scale events).

Appendix: quick mapping table (human-readable)
- Redwood: redwood_vpc.subnet_public -> Meridian: vlan_app_subnet_id
- Redwood: redwood_node_pool.gpu_type -> Meridian: meridian_gpu_node_pool.gpu_profile
- Redwood: storage.encryption_key -> Meridian: meridian_kms_integration.key_alias

If anything here needs to be turned into a formal SOW, flag it — this doc is intentionally technical and lightweight as a preflight; customer-facing proposal will follow once adapters and sizing validated in staging.
